about.title: The Greeks Who Taught Greek to the West, 1340s–1600
about.credit: A work in progress by Iosif Lazaridis (@iosif_lazaridis on X), supervising research by Anthropic's Claude, from public sources.
about.how_we_count:
- A manuscript counts if a source documents it in Latin Europe by 1600: an inventory or catalog made before 1600, an owner's note or arms before 1600, or a copy dated and placed in the West before 1600. "Latin Europe" is every territory under Latin bishops (all of Italy, Sicily included, after the Norman conquest; Spain; France; the German lands; England; Poland-Lithuania). Greek lands under Latin rule (Crete, Corfu, Cyprus, Rhodes, Chios, Naxos, Negroponte) stay the Greek world.
- A manuscript that is likely but not documented by 1600 is "probable" and is not counted.
- **Each book counts once.** Where an old inventory and a modern catalog describe the same library, the inventory entry is counted and the catalog gives it today's shelfmark when the two can be matched. A book from the catalog is added only if it cannot be one of the inventory's entries: it came after the inventory was made, or it belonged to a different collection. - Vatican: the inventory of 1475 (773 Greek books) is counted; 96 entries are matched to today's codices; 93 codices that came after 1475 are added; 451 codices of the old fund that were, or may have been, there in 1475 are not added, because they may be among the 677 entries still unidentified. - Paris: Catherine de' Medici's inventory of 1589 (604 Greek books, Cardinal Ridolfi's library) is counted; 264 entries are matched to Paris shelfmarks; the 273 other Paris manuscripts marked as hers are not added.
- Pinakes is not used.

versions.title: Madrid, Grottaferrata, Oxford, Berlin, London, Cambridge, Wolfenbüttel, the Corvina
notes: **Sources downloaded by Iosif from HathiTrust:** Iriarte, *Regiae Bibliothecae Matritensis codices graeci mss.* I (1769); Rocchi, *Codices Cryptenses* (1883).

**From archive.org:** Coxe's Bodleian Greek catalogs (1853–54: Barocci, Laud, Selden, Auctarium, Canonici), Molhuysen's Codices Scaligerani (1910), the Berlin Greek catalogs (1890, 1897), Warner and Gilson's Royal manuscripts (1921) and the Harleian catalog (vols. 1–2, 4), M. R. James' Corpus Christi and Gonville and Caius catalogs, Köhler's Wolfenbüttel Gudiani (1913), Fraknói's Bibliotheca Corvina (1927).
8,232 counted (+332); 6,722 with today's shelfmark; 2,359 probable (+569, mostly Barozzi's books and Grottaferrata's old stock).

107 Pellicier books identified in Berlin (shelfmarks given to his list); 37 Madrid and Grottaferrata books linked to dated copies already held; 13 books known only through Claude Naulot (who acquired Pellicier's library) taken as Pellicier's; 48 Wolfenbüttel records of version 0.6 replaced by Köhler's.

versions.title: Paris (Omont's Inventaire sommaire)
notes: **Source downloaded by Iosif from HathiTrust:** H. Omont, *Inventaire sommaire des manuscrits grecs de la Bibliothèque nationale*, parts 1–3 (1886–88).
7,900 manuscripts counted (+118); 6,385 with today's shelfmark; 1,790 probable.

264 of Catherine de' Medici's 604 books matched to Paris shelfmarks; 85 books of Jean Hurault de Boistaillé (d. 1572) and 14 more Fontainebleau books added; about 30 added on their own evidence; 13 double counts removed.

versions.title: the Vatican catalogs
notes: Devreesse (Vat. gr. 330–866), Schreiner (867–932), Giannelli (1485–1683), Canart's history of the later fund, Lilla (Columnenses; 2644–2663), Turyn (dated 13th–14th-c. codices), used for facts only.
7,782 counted (+283). 96 entries of the 1475 inventory matched. Correction: the Columnenses are Cardinal Giovanni Salviati's library (Matal's list of 1546), not Sirleto's.

versions.title: some 40 more public-domain catalogs
notes: Vat. gr. 1–329 (Mercati 1923); Florence, Rome, Modena, Bologna and other Italian libraries (Studi italiani di filologia classica); Martini's catalog and the Vallicelliana; Messina, San Salvatore; Turin; Tübingen (Crusius), Leiden (Vulcanius), Wolfenbüttel, Leipzig, Sweden, Copenhagen; the Arundel manuscripts and Cambridge; French provincial libraries; Omont's list of the scribes of the Paris fund; the papal library of 1295–1311; Reiser's Augsburg index of 1675.
7,499 counted (+1,017). Corrections: three copies made after 1600 and 23 Latin codices with a few Greek lines no longer count.

versions.title: Catherine de' Medici, Urbino, Ambrosiana I, Ottoboni, Reginenses
notes: 6,482 counted (+964). Correction: Sirleto's library went to Ascanio Colonna in 1588 and only in 1611 to Altemps, so Altemps-only books are probable.

versions.title: Palatine, Marciana, Vienna, Ambrosiana II, Switzerland, Spain and Portugal, Breslau, Oxford
notes: 5,518 counted (+1,514). Bessarion's deed of 1468 matched to Marciana shelfmarks (121 entries).

versions.title: the Laurentian, the Escorial, Munich; "the West" defined
notes: 4,004 counted. Iosif's ruling: the West is every territory under Latin bishops; Greek lands under Latin rule stay the Greek world.

versions.title: the first inventories
notes: Bessarion 1468, Fontainebleau c. 1550, Pellicier, the Vatican 1475, Orsini, Laskaris' purchases, Vogel and Gardthausen's dated scribes: 2,664 counted. Pinakes dropped; the four groups (a/b/c/d) adopted.

versions.title: people, editions, collections
notes: 120 people, 417 first editions, 52 collections; first estimate of 6,000–8,000 Greek manuscripts in Latin Europe by 1600.
